test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A pair of parallel lines is intersected by a transversal such that ∠1 and ∠2 form a pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal. If m∠1 = 65°, what is the measure of ∠2?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Interior angles on the same side** of a transversal (consecutive interior angles) between **parallel lines** are always **supplementary**.

Sum = 180°

∠2 = 180° − 65° = 115°

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lines are **parallel**.

m∠1 = 65°

∠1 and ∠2 are **interior angles** on the same side of the **transversal**.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of consecutive interior angles = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/80425589ae30d8e3237e3f1ed13e7ae32be1d21c6c285252dc7f9fd302c83dc7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ m∠1 + m∠2 = 180°

⇒ 65° + m∠2 = 180°

⇒ m∠2 = 180° − 65°

⇒ m∠2 = 115°

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Interior Angles

When parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, alternate interior angles are equal in measure.

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others are equal if the lines are parallel.

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal.</p
